Inside the theorem that inference is legitimate, but the objection's real point is that hypothesis (iii) is only verified for finite minimal transversals: Claim 3.2's proof passes to π(T)=∏_{p∈T}p and asks whether it lies in S_∞, which presupposes T finite (π is defined only for finite prime sets). Infinite minimal transversals of an intersecting antichain do exist in general (e.g. C={{1,k}:k≥2} has minimal transversal {2,3,4,...}), so the case is not vacuous. Hence Step 3 does not license the unrestricted (iii) that Step 4's decisive step uses, leaving the finiteness obligation unproved."}
